facts.text: The Jurassic Period lasted from about 201.4 million years ago to about 143.1 million years ago.
The Jurassic was the middle period of the Mesozoic Era, after the Triassic and before the Cretaceous.
The Jurassic is named after the Jura Mountains, where rocks from this period were studied.
At the beginning of the Jurassic, a major extinction had recently changed life on Earth.
During the Jurassic, the supercontinent Pangaea was beginning to split apart.
Pangaea split into northern Laurasia and southern Gondwana during the Jurassic.
By the end of the Jurassic, South America had begun to move away from Africa.
A narrow Atlantic Ocean began opening as Pangaea pulled apart.
The Jurassic climate was warmer than today's climate.
There were no ice caps during the Jurassic.
Jurassic plants included ferns, tree ferns, conifers, ginkgos, cycads, and horsetails.
The Morrison Formation preserves Late Jurassic river and floodplain habitats in western North America.
The Morrison Formation ecosystem included fish, frogs, salamanders, lizards, crocodiles, turtles, pterosaurs, small mammal relatives, and many dinosaurs.
On land, Jurassic animal life became dominated by dinosaurs.
The Jurassic saw sauropods become larger than any land animals that had lived before them.
Jurassic dinosaurs included long-necked sauropods, plated stegosaurs, meat-eating theropods, and early bird-like dinosaurs.
The Morrison Formation is one of North America's richest sources of dinosaur fossils.
Brachiosaurus lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 155.6 to 145.5 million years ago.
Brachiosaurus had longer front legs than back legs, giving its body a high-shouldered shape.
Brachiosaurus may have eaten plants as high as about 9 meters above the ground.
Brachiosaurus was a sauropod with a long neck, small skull, and huge body.
Apatosaurus lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 152 to 151 million years ago.
Apatosaurus was a large, four-legged sauropod with a long neck and a long whip-like tail.
Apatosaurus had a small skull compared with its huge body.
Apatosaurus ate plants.
Diplodocus lived in western North America near the end of the Jurassic Period.
Diplodocus was a very long sauropod with a long neck and an especially long tail.
Diplodocus carnegii is known from a nearly complete skeleton and could reach about 24 to 26 meters long.
Diplodocus had small peg-like teeth near the front of its jaws.
Stegosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, about 155 to 145 million years ago.
Stegosaurus had upright plates along its back and spikes near the end of its tail.
Scientists think Stegosaurus tail spikes were probably used for defense.
Stegosaurus was a plant-eating, four-legged dinosaur with a small head and short neck.
Allosaurus lived about 155 to 143 million years ago during the Late Jurassic.
Allosaurus was a large two-legged predator with a strong skull and many sharp serrated teeth.
Allosaurus had powerful hind legs, a long balancing tail, and three-fingered hands.
Allosaurus was one of the most common large predators in the Morrison Formation.
The first stem-group birds appeared during the Jurassic, evolving from theropod dinosaurs.
Archaeopteryx lived around 150 million years ago in what is now southern Germany.
Archaeopteryx was about the size of a magpie, with larger individuals perhaps about the size of a raven.
Archaeopteryx had feathers and wings, but also teeth, clawed fingers, and a long bony tail.
